category_title: Black girls with learning disabilities who use creative writing for self-advocacy
minimal_context: The student is using a Chromebook in Writing Club to draft a personal narrative about her grandmother.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today in Writing Club, please use your Chromebook to write the first draft of your personal narrative about your grandmother.

STUDENT: It’s just something that connects to me. I write a lot, something that I love.

TUTOR: That's good. Go ahead and type the beginning of your story.

STUDENT: My grand mother once had a twin but she past away and she had a husband named johny and everyone loved him but about time i was born he past away so i basicly grew up without a grandfather.

TUTOR: Keep writing, but make sure to check your spelling and how you organize your sentences.

STUDENT: But one day my mom dropped me and my big sister off at my grand moms house.so my sister was upstairs in my grand moms room watching tv and i was layin on the couch (just a baby) and my grand mom was in the kitchen with her mind distracted on cooking .Then i had fell off the couch, when she her a loud BANG,BOOM! she came running but she tripped over a bucket and fractured her leg but she told me later on in my life that she managed to get to me because she” loves me.”And that is one of the reasons why i love and admire my grandmother.

options.A: Ask all three types of follow-up questions (inference, justify, opinion) about the personal narrative within the same exchange.
options.B: Ask a follow-up question about the personal narrative that links the physical sensation described to a potential emotional state.
options.C: Encourage a sloppy first draft on the Chromebook that can be worked through together to revise and edit, focusing on authentic purposes for writing.
options.D: Ask the student what she is trying to compose in her personal narrative about her grandmother during this session.
